purpose: Local offline semantic regressions for independent editorial review; no automatic paid-model calibration, training or publication. Proposed negative facts are intentionally unsupported and must never be treated as source material.

value.paragraph: For the Lambayeque region around Motupe, a useful later context is the study of everyday life after conquest rather than a single ethnic label. Klaus (2016) brings documentary, archaeological and biological evidence together at Mórrope to investigate colonial changes in health, diet, physical activity, burial practice and identity. He also warns that European interpretations can obscure indigenous experience. His work opens questions about bodies, food and community beyond the conquerors’ narrative, but concerns Mórrope in 1536–1750; its abstract supplies neither a description of Motux in 1532 nor specific results that can safely be transferred there.
value.period_limits: Study scope 1536–1750, Mórrope in Lambayeque. Mórrope and Motupe are different places; regional relevance is contextual, not a claim of identical populations or practices.
value.source_viewpoint_limits: Klaus explicitly discusses European ethnocentrism and misinterpretation. The abstract describes research questions and methods; no particular diet, disease rate or burial result is asserted here.
value.historic_encounter_narrative: No claim that every Motux inhabitant was Muchik, Sicán or Lambayeque, and no reconstructed 1532 custom.

claims.claim: Mórrope study combines three evidence types to investigate bodies, diet, burials and identity.
European ethnocentrism can distort Andean interpretation.

contexts.value: Y preguntó el dicho Ynga a fray Uisente quién se lo auía dicho. Responde fray Uisente que le auía dicho euangelio, el libro. Y dixo Atagualpa: “Dámelo a mí el libro para que me lo diga.” Y ancí se la dio y lo tomó en las manos, comensó a oxear las ojas del dicho libro. Y dize el dicho Ynga: “¿Qué, cómo no me lo dize? ¡Ni me habla a mí el dicho libro!” Hablando con grande magestad, asentado en su trono, y lo echó el dicho libro de las manos el dicho Ynga Ataguálpa.
contexts.scope_limits: Later Indigenous author’s portrayal, not established verbatim speech in1532; dialogue alone does not establish psychology or authorial causal intent.
